key_insight: Concrete form of the solved-read thesis: 32-cell bitline (~1-1.5 fF real, not 0.05) lets a 0.2-0.3 fF stub replace the 1.3 um AR-60 pillar and VARY drop toward 0.4 V.
killer_doubt: Sense amp in ~0.04 um2: sigma-Vt ~40-60 mV vs ~100 mV signal; 6 decks need per-32-cell vias through 5 wafers; 0.3 fF needs IGZO (<1 fA tail).
decisive_experiment: 22/28 nm MPW (~$250k): arrays of offset-compensated micro-SAs in a 0.04-0.08 um2 footprint sensing 0.2-0.3 fF MIM cells on 1-1.5 fF bitlines; map offset and BER to 1e-6 at 85 C.
prior_art: IBM POWER7 eDRAM micro-SA (~32 cells/local bitline); Samsung 4F2 VCT periphery-under-cell via bonding; imec/EVG 200 nm W2W bond pitch (ECTC 2026, via search snippet).

key_insight: ~1.2B phones/yr at ~5-6 GB is ~7e9 GB, ~15-20% of world DRAM bit output, with zero wafer starts; at 4x prices a $20/GB bounty can raise collection.
killer_doubt: Realistic 15-20% collection x 70% rework yield gives ~1e9 GB (~3% supply); 3rd-4th reflow on MSL-3 PoP parts plus >50 ballout variants could push cost past $5/package.
decisive_experiment: Harvest 1,000 EOL phones (~$150k): measure desolder/bake/reball yield, retention and hammer (HCfirst) bins, all-in $/GB; run 16 packages behind an FPGA CXL Type-3 bridge with remap for 1,000 h.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU reuses retired DDR4 behind CXL; Shenzhen reballed/recycled DRAM trade (often counterfeit). Phone-LPDDR-to-CXL: none found.

key_insight: A capacity-tier spec grade that tolerates a raw fault rate lets the controller pay for weak cells and the retention tail, and ties to the ECC-paid capacitor (N-62).
killer_doubt: At 1% raw, each 64 B block has ~5 bad bits: BCH t>=12 costs >20% parity; LDPC needs ~4 kb codewords, breaking 64 B access. 1e-4 is just N-62.
decisive_experiment: Buy off-spec die (SpecTek-class bins), take fail bitmaps at 85 C, and classify random vs clustered faults; FPGA controller to test 64 B code overhead and latency at 1e-4/1e-3/1e-2 raw.
prior_art: Micron SpecTek sells off-spec DRAM; DDR5 on-die SEC ECC; Flikker/approximate DRAM; Phase B N-62 ECC-paid capacitor.

key_insight: No-refresh, no-restore ROM reads at ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit from idle mature-node capacity offload static weights from HBM without DRAM wafer starts.
killer_doubt: 2-bit via-ROM at 28 nm is ~50 Mb/mm2 vs 1b DRAM ~440: a 70B 4-bit model needs ~5,600 mm2; via mask ~$100-200k per model version against 3-12 month model churn.
decisive_experiment: 28 nm MPW (~$150k) of a via-programmed 2-bit ROM macro: measure bits/mm2, read pJ/bit and BER, then a model-churn cost model versus HBM $/GB at 2026 prices.
prior_art: Taalas hardwired-model inference chips (recalled, unverified); ROM-based compute-in-memory (e.g., YOLoC, DAC 2022); mask-ROM is textbook.

key_insight: An open periphery generator plus a pooled, documented expired-patent base lowers design and legal entry cost for allied DRAM entrants; demo is software only.
killer_doubt: The binding barrier is fab capital (~$15B) and process yield know-how, not IP. DRAM periphery is pitch-matched full-custom, and the big 3 are unlikely to donate live patents.
decisive_experiment: $300k: extend OpenRAM to generate an open-bitline DRAM row/column periphery for one open PDK; tape out a 1 Mb 1T1C-emulation test array on MPW; survey 5 would-be entrants on whether IP blocks them.
prior_art: OpenRAM (SRAM compiler); RISC-V and MPEG-LA pool models; CXMT acquired the Qimonda patent base for freedom to operate.

key_insight: Every pre-Nov-2006 patent has expired, so a 50-90 nm stacked-capacitor flow is largely free to operate; the atlas mainly removes legal fear.
killer_doubt: A 50-90 nm node gives ~0.02 Gb/mm2 vs 0.44 at 1b (~25x fewer bits per wafer): ~$20-40/GB cost, uncompetitive even at 4x prices. Subsumed by I-04102.
decisive_experiment: $50k: cost a 65 nm 1 Gb die (bits/wafer, $/GB) against $20/GB contract price before any legal work; if >$15/GB, stop.
prior_art: Commercial patent-landscape/FTO services; CXMT used the Qimonda portfolio. A public atlas: none found.

key_insight: Tacit yield know-how is real and scarce; structured capture could shorten a new entrant's learning curve.
killer_doubt: Tacit yield learning moves with teams, not transcripts (CXMT/JHICC hired retired engineers); expert networks already sell this at ~$1k/hour, and knowledge from 90-65 nm is ~6 nodes stale.
decisive_experiment: $100k: interview 20 retired integrators and test whether a new fab team solves 5 historical yield excursions faster with the knowledge base than without it.
prior_art: Computer History Museum oral histories; GLG-type expert networks; Chinese DRAM entrants recruiting retired Japanese/Taiwanese/Korean engineers.

key_insight: Idle-age tiered compression is pure logic and adds capacity without wafers.
killer_doubt: Fleet data show ~20-30% cold memory at ~3x compression, a ~15-25% saving, not 1.6-2.5x. Hyperscalers and CXL-compression vendors already ship it.
decisive_experiment: None needed beyond replaying a public memory trace (e.g., Google/Meta far-memory data) through an LZ4/zstd age ladder simulator, about $20k.
prior_art: Google software-defined far memory (zswap, ASPLOS 2019); Meta TMO (ASPLOS 2022); OCP hyperscale CXL tiered-memory expander with compression; ZeroPoint.

key_insight: A selective lateral recess, as in 3D NAND replacement gates, can contact alternating electrode sets from one trench without a high-AR hole etch.
killer_doubt: Geometric equivalence: one layer at 864 nm2 is ~0.06 fF, not 0.5. 5.4 fF needs ~90 layers (~1.2 um); per-cell isolation is an AR ~90 metal etch.
decisive_experiment: $80k nanofab: a 10-layer TiN/ZrO2/Ru stack, single trench, selective recess; measure C per layer, leakage per cell and recess uniformity. It shows the per-cell isolation etch is the wall.
prior_art: Fujitsu fin-type stacked capacitor (IEDM 1988: multiple horizontal fins); stacked BEOL MIM; horizontal capacitors in 3D DRAM.

key_insight: Idle 22-40 nm logic capacity and open PDKs could make embedded DRAM-class macros without DRAM fabs.
killer_doubt: Si gain cell at 28 nm: ~0.15 um2/bit (~50x 1b's 0.0023), ~10-100 us retention at 85 C; ~43 GB/wafer, ~$58/GB vs $20/GB contract. Not capacity tier.
decisive_experiment: Use existing OpenGCRAM/RAAAM silicon data to cost $/GB per wafer; only an IGZO BEOL module (N-43 class) changes the answer, so test IGZO 2T0C retention on a mature-node BEOL coupon.
prior_art: RAAAM Memory Technologies GCRAM IP for standard CMOS; OpenGCRAM open-source gain-cell compiler (recalled); imec IGZO 2T0C.

key_insight: Drawn coaxial metal/glass/metal cores yield ~1.5 fF/um, so a 100 um slice gives ~150 fF per core with no HAR etch. Capacitors are free; switches are not.
killer_doubt: Drawn chalcogenide/poly-Si switches leak decades above the ~1e-14 A needed; distorted fused lattices still need aligned litho; 1 um pitch is ~440x below 1b density.
decisive_experiment: $150k university draw tower: a fiber with a drawn semiconductor-core FET; measure Ion/Ioff and off-current at 85 C. Below 1e6 Ion/Ioff or above 1e-13 A off-current kills it.
prior_art: MIT Fink/Abouraddy multimaterial fibers, fiber diodes (Rein et al., Nature 2018); iterative-draw nanowires (Yaman et al., 2011).

key_insight: Vertical thin-film devices can take their channel length from film thickness, not litho, which is useful for tiered oxide cells, not PV lines.
killer_doubt: Scribe/print pitch of 20-50 um gives ~1e3 um2/bit, ~4e5x below 1b, not 500x: ~6 MB per wafer, ~$30/GB. At 5 um laser pitch, serial scribing takes ~1e3 s per wafer-layer.
decisive_experiment: Paper study ($10k): bits/wafer and $/GB versus scribe pitch and laser write speed, including periphery chips. This idea fails at every pitch reachable by PV tools.
prior_art: Display-fab TFT ICs (PragmatIC flexible ICs); TFT memory on glass. A PV-line memory: none found.
